verdict.rationale: Mercury ships several automation primitives that can run in the background — webhooks/events API for reactive automation, auto-invoicing, AI-driven receipt matching and bookkeeping sync, plus an official CLI/API usable from scripts or CI pipelines and an 'agent skills' repo for CLI-driven automations. However, the flagship agent-facing surface (the hosted MCP server) is explicitly read-only (31 get/list tools, no write actions), so autonomous write-side actions (payments, invoices) would have to go through the API/CLI/webhooks rather than a persistent scheduled agent runtime, and no dedicated scheduler/cron/'run this automation on a trigger' product feature is documented. Missing for 10: a first-party scheduling/trigger engine for autonomous multi-step workflows, evidence of write-capable autonomous agent execution, and independent confirmation that background automations run reliably unattended.
